requirements.requirement: Configure opsadmin on node1 for SSH access with the specified ed25519 public key
requirements.summary: cmd-58d4636dd7c84b12 shows opsadmin user created and /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys populated with exactly the requested key, permissions 700/600 owned by opsadmin. cmd-657dc563e248495f (post-reboot) confirms the user, key, and permissions are intact after a genuine reboot, demonstrating durable configuration rather than a transient in-memory change.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based SSH authentication (disable password/interactive auth)
requirements.summary: cmd-58d4636dd7c84b12 deploys /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-ssh-key-only.conf with PubkeyAuthentication yes and PasswordAuthentication/ChallengeResponseAuthentication/KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, validated with sshd -t and confirmed via sshd -T effective output. cmd-335264afb0104768 re-confirms this pre-restart, and cmd-657dc563e248495f confirms the same effective policy persists after a real reboot, showing the hardening is persistent rather than only in the running process.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/config state
requirements.summary: cmd-d64d2cac100f41bc and cmd-335264afb0104768 capture pre-restart boot_id (1b0321bf...) and healthy sshd/config state. cmd-41a2ef8d4ec04410 issues a non-blocking reboot with acknowledgement. cmd-5a2d06f5906444e3 shows a timeout (node down), cmd-549b3fffc0c745c9 shows the node reachable again. cmd-657dc563e248495f shows a new boot_id (7ef2e674...), uptime reset to 0 minutes, and full recovery of sshd, opsadmin user, key, permissions, and the key-only auth policy. This matches the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot (7ef2e674-b659-498d-9961-d4c065627d7f), independently corroborating the transition.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes (opsadmin configured with the specified key, and key-based SSH auth enforced) are directly and persistently satisfied, verified both before and after a genuine, evidence-backed reboot. The independent node-restart protocol is also fully satisfied with a clean pre/post transition (boot_id change, uptime reset, full service/config/data recovery) corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or residue were found.
limitations: Evidence relies on sshd -T output and file contents rather than an actual external SSH login attempt with the provided key or a password, so end-to-end authentication behavior was not directly exercised.
Command outputs are executor-reported and not independently re-verified by the verifier beyond cross-checking against the fixed lifecycle snapshots for boot identity.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 7 executor commands in order. cmd-d64d2cac100f41bc, cmd-335264afb0104768, cmd-5a2d06f5906444e3, cmd-549b3fffc0c745c9, and cmd-657dc563e248495f are read-only discovery/verification. cmd-58d4636dd7c84b12 is the single state-changing setup command (user creation, key install, sshd hardening config, sshd restart) directly implementing the task requirements. cmd-41a2ef8d4ec04410 (systemctl reboot) is a state-changing action but is the mandatory restart-evidence action, bounded and expected. No unnecessary mutations, abandoned files, or failed services were found; the lifecycle diff shows only expected changes (new boot_id, new ephemeral systemd-private tmp dirs, new sshd/chronyd PIDs after reboot) with no residue or exposure changes. UsePAM yes was included in the sshd drop-in as a standard companion setting, not a harmful addition.
